description: Agent Customs Records: submit country-of-origin and marking records with the invoices and origin support they answer to: each entry with its id, entry number, the country of origin declared, the trade program whose preference rate it claims, the origin certificate or statement it cites, any marking exception recorded and the basis noted for it; each commercial invoice line with its id, the entry and the country of origin it states; each origin certificate or statement on file with its id, reference, the origin it certifies and the program it supports; each change to an origin record after entry with its id, the entry, the moment changed, the origin before and after and the amendment it records; each amendment or post-entry correction with its id, reference, the entry and the moment filed. The signed report gives the entries and the claims, each declared origin against the invoice lines, each preference claim against the origin support on file, each marking exception against its noted basis, and each origin change against an amendment recorded for its entry, and counts them, and names divergent country-of-origin records: origin declared differently on the entry and the invoice, a preference claim at a trade-program rate recorded with no origin support on file, a marking exception recorded with no basis noted, and an origin record changed after entry with no amendment recorded; then an invoice line naming an entry the records do not hold and a certificate stating another origin or program than the claim it supports, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No entries, an entry with no country of origin, or no invoice lines leaves those points unverified. Entries, invoice lines, certificates and amendments match by letters and digits, an amendment only for its own entry, and countries compare by name or two-letter code without case or punctuation, so China, PRC and CN are one origin. This reads where the importer’s own records say the goods were made and how they are marked. Verdict customs_origin_divergent, customs_origin_partial, customs_origin_unverified or customs_origin_consistent. POST /api/customs-origin-check. Reads the customs and trade records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads the records as supplied only: it files no entry, pays no duty, contacts no customs authority or broker and gives no customs or legal advice, which stay with the importer, its licensed customs broker and its advisers, and the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Customs Records reads an importer’s or exporter’s own customs and trade records: entry summaries, tariff classification records, duty and fee payment records, broker filing records, country-of-origin and marking records, declared-value records, customs bond records and drawback claim records, each against the commercial invoices and duty payment records, the rulings on file, the entries, the importer’s own copies, the origin support on file, the invoices and payments, the entry activity or the duty recorded as paid and the proof on file. The family’s ground is the paper behind the border crossing: what was declared, how it was classified, what duty was paid, and whether the bond and the drawback claims line up; the Agent Tax Records family reads filings made to the tax authority, and the Agent Logistics family reads where a shipment is and when it moves, while this family reads neither. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-customs-records-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-customs-records/.
